llamacpp_tp2_model.note: llama.cpp TP=2 shards attention as well as the MLP, so its per-layer path is attention_half + mlp_half + two reduces. Applying that decomposition to the measured hipEngine phases predicts the measured llama.cpp time only if its per-layer reduce is cheaper than ours.

findings: The attention phase is fully replicated: _bulk_attention_layer calls the full-width _run_full_attention_prefill_attn_rows / _run_linear_attention_prefill_attn_rows, which read out_features=2*q_width and the unsharded attn_q/k/v/output weights, so both ranks execute identical attention work.
The attention phase is device-bound, not enqueue-bound: 233.39 ms of device span against 78.30 ms of host span.
The 48 linear-attention (GDN) layers carry 180.99 ms of the 233.63 ms attention phase (77.5%); the 16 full-attention layers carry 52.64 ms.

Attention is GEMM-bound, not kernel-bound: per-layer rates are 31.7 TFLOP/s (GDN) and 34.6 TFLOP/s (full attention) against 46.5 TFLOP/s for the sharded MLP chain at the even split's 8704-wide shard, so the projections dominate the phase and a head split halves them.

Device 0 (W7900) is the pacer at every replicated phase (attention 233.39 vs 208.86; chain 188.43 vs 168.04), so the even split makes the slower card the pacer and device 1 absorbs the imbalance as 45.9 ms of extra spin wait inside mlp_exchange.

The 0.93 ms/layer mlp_exchange moves 5.24 MB per rank per direction (bf16 partial, 512x5120) at about 11.3 GB/s of PCIe traffic, at or above the host's measured staged-collective rate (7.09 GB/s all_reduce:rows1024:bf16; 11.52 GB/s broadcast:rows1024:fp32 in benchmarks/results/tp2_collective_bench.json). The reduce is near the platform floor rather than a fixable inefficiency.

Superseded: the note that replicated GDN/attention is 'only ~7% of profiled kernel time' counted the attention kernel alone, not the replicated q/k/v and output projections that make up most of the phase.

The whole 104.8 ms gap decomposes into unsharded attention (117 ms of replicated work that a head split removes for one added reduce) and a per-layer reduce that is 0.38 ms more expensive than the 0.55 ms/layer llama.cpp's measured 385.4 ms implies.
limits: Stream-event spans, not kernel traces: a device span includes any bubble inside the phase. The host/device span ratio separates the two, and attention's host span is 3x smaller than its device span.

The sharding upside is an upper bound: half the attention phase minus one added reduce of the measured mlp_exchange size. It does not model the smaller GEMM shapes a head split produces, which will cost some efficiency.
Single shape (512 tokens), single split (even), c=1. Not a prompt-length scaling or quality result.
